newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RURAL PRESS SAYS HAS NOT SOLD RADIO ASSETS.
newsitem.headline: RURAL PRESS SAYS HAS NOT SOLD RADIO ASSETS.

text.p: Publisher Rural Press Ltd said on Wednesday while it had held talks over the last two years on the sale of its radio assets, no deal had been concluded.

Replying to an Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) query, the company said it was unaware of any reason for recent rises in the share price, although it noted recent media coverage of the potential sale of its own and its competitors' radio networks.
Rural Press's share price rose to a record high A$4.66 on August 11 from A$4.00 on June 27, the period under question by the ASX.

The company also said the assimilation of its June 30 announcement of the acquisition of the U.S.-based agricultural publisher Farm Progress Group for US$56.9 million may explain the share price moves.
By 12.40 p.m. (0240 GMT), Rural Press shares were steady at A$4.60 after just two trades totalling 1,000 shares.
